observation_summary: The compiler was ignoring dependency management options when the compilation level was set to WHITESPACE_ONLY, causing dependency sorting to fail in tests.
hypothesis: The compiler's dependency management logic contained an overly restrictive condition (!options.skipAllPasses) that prevented dependency sorting from executing when it should have been enabled for WHITESPACE_ONLY mode.
prediction: Removing the !options.skipAllPasses check from the dependency management condition in the Compiler class will allow the dependency sorting logic to execute correctly in WHITESPACE_ONLY mode.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the removal of the !options.skipAllPasses condition, which directly confirms that this guard was preventing the intended dependency management logic from running.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic 'Checking' defect where an incorrect guard condition (!options.skipAllPasses) prevented a necessary feature (dependency management) from executing in a specific compilation mode. The fix was to remove this incorrect predicate, allowing the code to proceed as intended.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not a change to the sorting algorithm itself, but rather the removal of a guard that prevented the algorithm from being invoked.
This is not a missing design capability; the capability existed but was incorrectly gated by a condition.
